evidence.excerpt: Divergent releases and listings, June 2026: Lukas Czinger, President & Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder; Kevin Czinger, Founder, Lead Inventor & Executive Chairman; Cooper Keller promoted to Chief Operating Officer (1 Jun 2026); Ben Nicholson appointed Chief Commercial Officer (15 Jun 2026, from Ursa Major); Brian Erhartic named Chief Technology Officer (8 Jun 2026). No chief marketing officer and no CFO are named on any listing found.

Divergent, 17 Jun 2026 (PR Newswire; TCT, Metal AM, Breaking Defense, Long Beach Post): Monolith One is a laser powder-bed fusion printer with twelve 2kW lasers (24kW) and a 700 x 700 x 835 mm build volume, 28 months in development under CTO Brian Erhartic; a second factory of 430,000 sq ft in Long Beach, California, will house 64 Monolith One printers, raise annual production output 8X for defence and commercial programmes, create about 1,000 jobs and start production in the first half of 2027. CEO Lukas Czinger: the factory 'represents the new industrial age at scale'.

Divergent, 15 Sep 2025 (company release; SiliconANGLE, TechCrunch): closed a $290 million Series E at a $2.3 billion valuation, $250 million equity and $40 million debt, led by Rochefort Asset Management (which contributed $120 million), to scale manufacturing capacity and fund new product families.
Divergent, Nov 2023: closing of an upsized $230 million Series D. Tracxn and Crunchbase put total funding at about $1.1 billion as of July 2026 (reported).

McLaren Automotive release (Automotive World; TCT; Metal AM): a multi-year collaboration with Divergent; the McLaren W1's Formula 1-inspired front suspension uses Divergent's Adaptive Production System for the titanium front upper wishbone, aero-form lower wishbone and front upright, printed by Divergent, allowing rapid design iteration for stiffness and durability.

Divergent boilerplate, June 2026: founded in 2014, headquartered in Torrance, California; DAPS is an end-to-end digital manufacturing platform (AI-enabled design, additive manufacturing, automated assembly); contracts across aerospace, defence and automotive with Lockheed Martin, RTX, McLaren, Aston Martin, General Atomics, Bugatti, Saab and Triumph Group, delivering 600+ unique parts. Series E coverage: seven blue-chip automotive customers including Aston Martin and Mercedes-AMG.

Breaking Defense, June 2026: Divergent will print a key structure of the Tomahawk cruise missile at the Long Beach factory from 2027; capacity of upward of 30,000 missile airframes or 60,000 warhead casings a year; CEO Lukas Czinger describes Divergent as complementary supply for Raytheon.

Czinger Vehicles is Divergent's hypercar subsidiary (Lukas Czinger founder and CEO, Kevin Czinger founder and executive chairman); the 21C set production-car lap records at Laguna Seca and at the Circuit of the Americas and a production-car hillclimb record at the Goodwood Festival of Speed.

McLaren Racing, 2025: CYVN Holdings acquired McLaren Automotive and a non-controlling stake in McLaren Racing; Bahrain Mumtalakat remains majority shareholder of McLaren Racing, which stays operationally separate from McLaren Automotive under Zak Brown as CEO.

McLaren Racing partner page: Stratasys is the team's polymer 3D-printing supplier (FDM and PolyJet parts, trackside printing); reported still active in March 2026. Not listed as active in the sponsor table; a polymer-printing supplier, not a metal-structures or digital-manufacturing partner.

Sponsor table: McLaren F1 Team 2026 — Mastercard (title), Dell Technologies, Cisco, Google Cloud, Groq, Arrow Electronics, Greene Tweed, Smartsheet, Workday and others; no additive-manufacturing or digital-manufacturing partner active. Alpine: 3D Systems (additive). Audi: Additive Industries departed within the last 12 months; Camozzi active. Haas: Haas Automation (machine tools), Toyota Gazoo Racing (title). Red Bull: Siemens, Ansys. Cadillac: Tenneco, General Motors.
2026 F1 calendar table: British GP (Silverstone) in early July, Dutch GP and Italian GP (Monza) in late August and early September, US GP (Austin) in October and Las Vegas GP in November.

brief.industry_meta: Digital Manufacturing · AI Design + Metal Additive + Robotic Assembly
brief.deck: Divergent, the Torrance digital-manufacturing company whose printed titanium suspension sits on the McLaren W1, unveiled Monolith One, a twelve-laser metal printer, and a 430,000 sq ft second factory in Long Beach on 17 June 2026, an 8X step in output nine months after a $290M Series E at $2.3B.
brief.the_case_p1: On 17 June Divergent announced Monolith One, a laser powder-bed printer with twelve 2kW lasers, and a second factory: 430,000 sq ft in Long Beach, California, 64 printers, production from early 2027, an 8X rise in annual output. It follows the $290M Series E closed on 15 September 2025 at a $2.3B valuation, led by Rochefort Asset Management, after a $230M Series D in November 2023. The platform, DAPS, pairs AI-enabled design with metal additive and robotic assembly, and has delivered 600+ unique parts for Lockheed Martin, RTX, McLaren, Aston Martin and Bugatti.
brief.the_case_p2: Divergent already builds the McLaren W1's Formula 1-inspired front suspension: titanium upper and lower wishbones and the upright, printed by Divergent under a multi-year collaboration with McLaren Automotive. The road-car side of the brand is a customer; the racing side, operationally separate under Zak Brown, is not yet a partner. A second factory needs a flagship to fill it, and a race car is the fastest proof a structural printer can give.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The factory and the printer were announced on 17 June, with a new COO, CTO and Chief Commercial Officer named in the same month: a company staffing up to sell capacity. Silverstone falls days after the row; Monza and Austin sit inside the window, and 2027 rosters close in the fourth quarter.
brief.why_team_para: McLaren's roster is engineering-led, Dell, Cisco, Google Cloud, Groq, Arrow Electronics, but carries no additive or digital-manufacturing partner; Stratasys supplies polymer printing, a different lane from metal structures. The warm path is real: McLaren Automotive's engineers iterated the W1 wishbones on DAPS, and CYVN, which owns Automotive, holds a non-controlling stake in Racing. Alpine has 3D Systems and Haas is owned by a machine-tool brand; McLaren is where the printed-suspension story lives.
brief.value_section_label: VALUE TO MCLAREN MASTERCARD F1 TEAM
brief.value_content: MODE A - operational. Titanium uprights, wishbone prototypes, brackets and cooling manifolds designed with DAPS' AI-enabled optimisation and printed on Monolith One, with robotic assembly for sub-structures: the workflow that produced the W1's suspension, applied to a race car's fast-iteration parts inside the cost cap. McLaren gets shorter design-to-track cycles and a US manufacturing source; Divergent gets a flagship for the new factory.
brief.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Digital Manufacturing Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, spanning the Long Beach ramp. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-payable in printed parts and engineering time. Scope: sidepod placement, naming of a printed-structures programme, MTC content, hospitality at Silverstone, Austin and Las Vegas.
brief.decision_maker_bio: Czinger co-founded Divergent with his father Kevin, Executive Chairman, and runs Czinger Vehicles, whose 21C holds production-car lap records; a first F1 deal is his call. Path: Ben Nicholson, Chief Commercial Officer since 15 June, and Cooper Keller, COO. No CMO or CFO is listed.
brief.opening_angle_quote: “Lukas, your titanium wishbones already carry a McLaren; the Formula 1 team that inspired them has no manufacturing partner, and you have a factory to fill. 25 minutes before Silverstone to talk about a printed-structures programme?”
score_cells: $2.3B valuation, $290M Series E: mid-tier partner money.
Motorsport-native manufacturing story; defence identity dilutes.
Capacity to sell from 2027; no hard deadline.
MODE A: metal additive structures, proven on the W1.
risks: The June story is Tomahawk airframes; a weapons-manufacturing partner may not suit McLaren's consumer-facing brand mix.
Build the programme on the automotive lineage, W1, Bugatti, Aston Martin, and keep the activation technical.
McLaren Automotive is the customer; McLaren Racing is a different company with its own commercial team and top-of-grid pricing.
Use the Automotive engineers as the reference; enter at technology-partner level, part-paid in parts.
brief.bottom_line: A $2.3B company that already prints the McLaren W1's suspension has just announced a twelve-laser printer and a 430,000 sq ft factory it must fill. McLaren Racing carries no manufacturing partner, the warm path runs through McLaren Automotive's own engineers, and Silverstone opens the window days after the row.

The release is Divergent's own; TCT, Metal AM, Breaking Defense and the Long Beach Post carried it.

why_now.label: Capital already in place

The thin row scored the Series E as the trigger; it is nine months old. The fresh event is the factory, funded by that round.

why_now.label: A leadership team built in one month

A company that hires its first CCO in the month it announces a factory is about to sell capacity, and a brand partnership is part of how it does that.

why_now.label: Calendar window
why_now.text: The British GP at Silverstone falls days after the row, the Dutch and Italian GPs inside the six-to-ten-week window, and the US GP in Austin and the Las Vegas GP later in the year on Divergent's home ground. Teams close 2027 rosters in the fourth quarter.

why_team.label: The open lane
why_team.text: McLaren's 2026 roster is engineering-heavy, Dell Technologies, Cisco, Google Cloud, Groq, Arrow Electronics, Greene Tweed, Smartsheet, Workday, but the sponsor table shows no additive-manufacturing or digital-manufacturing partner. Stratasys supplies the team's polymer printing; metal structural components and robotic assembly are a different lane.

why_team.label: The warm path
why_team.text: McLaren Automotive's engineers worked with Divergent on the W1's titanium front upper wishbone, aero-form lower wishbone and front upright, printed by Divergent under a multi-year collaboration. McLaren Racing is a separate company, majority-owned by Bahrain Mumtalakat with CYVN Holdings, the owner of Automotive, holding a non-controlling stake, so the introduction runs through engineers who already trust the parts, not through a shared commercial team.

why_team.label: Why not the alternatives
why_team.text: Alpine carries 3D Systems as its additive partner. Haas is owned by a machine-tool brand, Haas Automation, whose identity a digital-manufacturing partner would cut across. Audi's Additive Industries relationship ended within the last 12 months, so the lane is open there, but Audi has no Divergent lineage. Aston Martin's road-car arm used DAPS for the DBR22 subframe and Mercedes-AMG is a customer too, so both are credible second choices; McLaren is where a live production programme already sits.

why_team.label: Story fit
why_team.text: The W1's suspension is described by McLaren as Formula 1-inspired. Putting the company that prints it onto the Formula 1 car closes the loop in a single sentence, and gives McLaren's technology-forward identity a manufacturing chapter it currently lacks.

value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)
value.text: Titanium uprights, wishbone prototypes, brackets, cooling manifolds and wind-tunnel-model structures designed with DAPS' AI-enabled optimisation and printed on Monolith One, with robotic assembly for sub-structures. It is the workflow that produced the W1's suspension, applied to a race car's fast-iteration parts; the value to the team is shorter design-to-track cycles and a second, US-based source of structural parts inside the cost cap.

value.label: Commercial lift for the team
value.text: Divergent's customers are aerospace primes, defence contractors and hypercar makers; its guest list at Austin and Las Vegas is an industrial and capital-markets audience that McLaren's technology partners want to meet.

value.label: Content and ecosystem
value.text: From metal powder to wishbone to race car: co-produced engineering content from the McLaren Technology Centre and Long Beach, a Formula 1 reference for Divergent's automotive sales, and a hypercar-to-F1 story through Czinger Vehicles, whose 21C holds production-car lap records.

value.label: What the team gives back

# Divergent Technologies → McLaren Mastercard F1 Team — verification log (N° 177, row of 27 Jun 2026)

Built in-session at no API cost (no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the sandbox) from a case spec: Claude did the research and writing; the pipeline's code stages (freshness, dedup, scoring, the claims ledger with calendar and sponsor-table checks, the 13-rule audit, the 2-page render, the app page) ran unchanged via `python -m intel.session_case`. ## The trigger, corrected

The thin row's trigger — "Series E reported to value Divergent at $2.3B" — is real but stale: the round closed on 15 September 2025, 285 days before the row. The row is kept because a fresh, company-announced inflection exists inside the window: on 17 June 2026 Divergent unveiled Monolith One and a 430,000 sq ft second factory in Long Beach for an 8X rise in output, with a COO (1 Jun), CTO (8 Jun) and Chief Commercial Officer (15 Jun) named the same month. `signal_date` is 17 Jun 2026 and the brief says the Series E is nine months old. The thin row's person (Lukas Czinger) is correct; his title on Divergent's releases is President & Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder.

## Team choice

The thin row hinted McLaren; the sponsor table supports it. McLaren Racing carries no additive or digital-manufacturing partner; Stratasys, McLaren's polymer-printing supplier, is not in the table as active and was reported still active in March 2026 — the brief names it and treats it as a different lane (polymer parts, not metal structures), which is stated honestly rather than hidden. McLaren Automotive's W1 uses Divergent-printed titanium suspension, and McLaren Racing is a separate company (Mumtalakat majority, CYVN non-controlling, operationally separate) — the brief says so and the second risk row is about exactly that. Alpine (3D Systems) and Haas (Haas Automation) are ruled out by name; Audi, Aston Martin, Mercedes, Cadillac and the Red Bull teams are addressed on the app page.
